# Uranium Sector Update

Report 066 | Published 2021-09-05 | Evaluated 2026-11-07

[Original member article](https://www.lynalden.com/premium-2021-9-5/) | [Article index](README.md) | [Structured review](../data/reviews/066.json)

Stagflation, crypto differentiation, and uranium.

The uranium commodity threshold and Solana/Cardano ranking call were supported; moving away from BlockFi removed a subsequently realized counterparty risk. High-debt constraints on the Fed were overstated. The strongest uranium explanation separates mine-output deficits, finite inventories and new financial buying, but exact depletion timing and causal price attribution remain uncertain.

**Coverage:** Read all blocks 0-214 and 26 image labels. Covers labor/policy explanations, crypto adoption/architecture, NFT critique, BlockFi exit, uranium mechanisms and selected inflation beneficiaries. Excludes routine holdings and incidental prices.

2014 Q1 bulletin: bank lending creates deposits; reserves are not multiplied into loans. QE can buy from nonbanks, directly increasing their deposits as well as bank reserves.

Bank-transaction difference-in-differences study of 16,253 recipients: benefit receipt declined 36.3 percentage points, employment rose 6.8 pp by early September; cumulative benefits fell $2,529, earnings rose $292. Ending aid did increase employment but did not replace lost income broadly.

At fixed NAV, an 11% premium falling to zero produces 9.91% loss: 1/1.11-1. This proves the isolated premium effect, not the probability or timing of reversion.

**Direction:** Supported for the defined proposition.

**Timing:** No fixed deadline stated.

**Mechanism:** Evaluate the explanation separately from subsequent price direction.

**Reviewer confidence:** high

**Deductive assessment:**

- NAV constant
- No distributions/fees during comparison
- Premium falls from11% to0%

Price 0=1.11*NAV; price 1=NAV; return=1/1.11-1=-9.9099%.

**Outcome evidence:**

No independent outcome source is recorded. Any deductive assessment is identified separately.
